title: Streamlining financial regulation while safeguarding stability and tackling new risks
summary: BIS General Manager Pablo Hernández de Cos delivered a speech on March 4, 2026 examining post-GFC regulatory reforms and their outcomes. The speech highlights that banking sector resilience has markedly improved with CET1 ratios rising to 14.3% (from under 10% in 2011) and discusses the rationale for reviewing and potentially streamlining existing regulatory frameworks while preserving financial stability. The speech frames three key questions for assessing post-crisis reforms and notes that the current framework has focused primarily on banking sector regulation while non-bank financial intermediaries remain less comprehensively covered.
key_points: Post-GFC reforms have significantly strengthened banking sector capital positions: CET1 ratios stand at 14.3% versus under 10% in 2011, and equity-to-assets ratio increased from 3.5% to 6.1%

Liquidity positions have improved substantially: high-quality liquid assets increased 55% between 2012-2025 (now 21% of total), and stable funding increased nearly 40% to approximately 56% of total exposures
The banking system has successfully weathered successive shocks including Covid-19, Russia-Ukraine war economic reverberations, and 2023 banking turmoil
Post-crisis reforms focused mainly on the banking sector while non-bank financial intermediary (NBFI) regulation has been strengthened much less

Three assessment questions proposed: (i) whether reforms achieved resilience objectives, (ii) whether resilience can be preserved while improving efficiency, and (iii) whether current framework can handle evolving risks
Financial stability is characterized as a global public good requiring cross-border cooperation to prevent regulatory fragmentation, arbitrage, and potential race-to-the-bottom dynamics
why_it_matters: This speech provides an authoritative BIS perspective on the state of global banking regulation 20 years after the GFC. It signals that policymakers are now entering a phase of evaluating whether regulatory frameworks can be streamlined without compromising resilience—a potential signal for future regulatory policy direction. The emphasis on NBFI risks and the three-question framework for assessment suggests areas where regulatory attention may shift.
macro_context: The speech discusses the resilience of the global financial system and the case for ongoing regulatory evaluation. It positions financial stability as a global public good requiring international cooperation. While not directly market-moving, the speech signals a potential policy direction toward regulatory streamlining that could affect compliance costs and competitive dynamics across the banking sector.
market_structure_context: While the speech discusses financial system structure through the lens of regulatory frameworks, it does not address market operations, trading mechanics, plumbing, or execution venue structure. It focuses on prudential regulation of banks rather than market microstructure.

Stable funding: approximately 56% of total exposures, +40% increase since 2012
